seo.title: What is a content delivery network?
seo.description: A content delivery network is a set of servers spread around the world that serve copies of your files from somewhere near each visitor.

definition: A content delivery network is a set of servers spread around the world that serve copies of your files from somewhere near each visitor.
answerBlock: A content delivery network is a set of servers spread around the world that serve copies of your files from somewhere near each visitor. Distance costs time, so a file travelling from the same city arrives sooner than one crossing a continent. Images, stylesheets and scripts are the usual candidates.

body.heading: What does a CDN change in practice?
paragraphs: Two things: the distance a file travels, and how often your own server is asked for it at all. A cached copy near the visitor answers immediately, and your server handles only the requests that genuinely need it.

A CDN does not fix a slow page on its own. If the largest element on the page is a hero image that is four times larger than it needs to be, delivering that image from nearby only makes it slightly less slow. Caching rules matter too: a poorly configured cache can serve yesterday's price list.
Most CDNs also absorb traffic spikes and filter obvious abuse before it reaches your infrastructure, which is worth as much as the speed on the day a campaign lands.

commercial.heading: Why does it matter commercially?
paragraphs: For a business selling in more than one region, the difference between a local and a transcontinental round trip is visible in Largest Contentful Paint, which is one of the measures Google uses to describe page experience.
It also makes launches less frightening: the expensive part of a traffic spike is served from cache rather than from your database.

example.heading: What does it look like in practice?
example.body: A campaign landing page with a background video serves the poster image and the video from a nearby edge, so a visitor on a hotel connection sees the hero immediately rather than waiting for a file from another continent.

service.title: Website care plans
service.line: Patching, backups with a tested restore, monitoring and a fixed allowance of development hours.

terms.definition: A backup is a copy of the site and its database held somewhere else, and a restore is the rehearsed process of putting that copy back.
DNS is the system that turns a domain name someone types into the address of the server that answers for it.
A staging environment is a private copy of the live site where changes are tested before anyone outside the company sees them.
A TLS certificate is the file that lets a website prove who it is and encrypt the traffic between it and the visitor.
